name: Carapace
vibe_summary: A security-hardened Rust rewrite of the OpenClaw personal assistant concept, built explicitly to counter the January 2026 OpenClaw vulnerability disclosures. It pairs a signed WASM plugin runtime with OS-level sandboxing and encrypted secret storage for a genuinely locked-down local agent.
best_for: Security-conscious users who want an OpenClaw-style assistant without its exposed attack surface
Self-hosters who want multi-channel messaging (Matrix, Signal, Telegram, Discord, Slack) with local-first defaults
Rust developers who want a signed, sandboxed WASM plugin model
avoid_if: You need a large plugin/skill ecosystem like OpenClaw's 5,000+ skills registry
You want a mature community, mobile apps, or a polished control UI
You need features still marked partial in its feature-status docs
openclaw_advantages: OS-level subprocess sandboxing with fail-closed behavior on unsupported paths
Ed25519-signed WASM plugins with capability sandboxing and resource limits
Secrets in OS credential stores with AES-256-GCM fallback instead of plaintext
Localhost-only binding, CSRF protection, and SSRF/DNS-rebinding defenses by default
Rust memory safety plus active fuzzing and cargo audit hygiene
openclaw_disadvantages: Tiny community (47 stars) versus OpenClaw's massive user base and skill registry
No mobile apps, Canvas, or polished Control UI
Some features explicitly marked partial or in-progress
No third-party security audit evidence beyond self-published docs
confidence_summary: README and commit history give strong evidence of active, security-focused engineering, but community sentiment is essentially unmeasurable — all 18 Reddit matches are unrelated uses of the word 'carapace'. Feature-completeness claims rely on the project's own status docs.

overview_markdown:
Carapace is a security-first, Rust-based personal AI assistant positioned as a hardened alternative to OpenClaw/Clawdbot. It supports a broad multi-provider LLM engine (Anthropic, OpenAI, Codex, Ollama, Gemini, Vertex AI, Bedrock, NEAR AI, Venice AI, and local Claude CLI) and connects to Matrix, Signal, Telegram, Discord, Slack, webhooks, and console channels, with per-channel typing indicators and read receipts.

Its defining trait is the security architecture, designed threat-by-threat against the January 2026 OpenClaw disclosures: localhost-only binding, CSRF-protected control endpoints, OS credential-store secret storage with AES-256-GCM fallback, Ed25519-signed WASM plugins running under capability sandboxes with resource limits, prompt-injection defenses (prompt guard, inbound classifier, exec approval flow), OS-level subprocess sandboxing that fails closed on unsupported paths, and SSRF/DNS-rebinding mitigation. Infrastructure extras include TLS/mTLS, mDNS discovery, Tailscale integration, Prometheus metrics, and audit logging.

Compared to OpenClaw, Carapace trades ecosystem breadth for rigor: there is no giant skill registry, mobile app, or Control UI, and the project transparently tracks verified-vs-partial features in docs/feature-status.yaml. Recent commits show disciplined maintenance — grouped Dependabot updates, fuzz-lock hygiene, RUSTSEC advisory remediation, and a 4,900+ test suite — suggesting a small but serious engineering effort rather than a vibe-coded fork.
